# Notification of Claimed Infringement (DMCA Takedown)

## When to use this

Use this when a work the Kingdom owns is being hosted, displayed, or distributed
by a third party through an online service — a website host, a social platform, a
marketplace, a video service — and the Kingdom wants it removed without a lawsuit.
The notice is addressed to the *service provider*, never to the infringer. It
works because the provider's own safe harbour under 17 U.S.C. § 512 depends on
acting expeditiously once it receives a compliant notice, so the provider's
interests and the Kingdom's briefly align.

This is rung three of the escalation ladder in `02-IP-ENFORCEMENT-PLAYBOOK`. Most
matters end here, at no cost, within days. Do not use it against a member or an
admirer who would take the material down if asked (rung two), against a critic or
a journalist (section 7 of the playbook), or on a work the Kingdom has not
registered — because a counter-notice will force a decision to sue that
17 U.S.C. § 411(a) makes impossible on an unregistered work.

## Before you send

- [ ] **The Kingdom owns the work, or holds an exclusive licence in it.** Only the
      owner of an *exclusive* right, or a person authorised to act for that owner,
      may send this notice. A non-exclusive licensee may not. Confirm the chain of
      title in the Register of Rights: named author, named owner, and the signed
      writing transferring it if the author was not the Kingdom (17 U.S.C.
      § 204(a)). Where the volunteer who made the seal or the contractor who wrote
      the site has not signed an assignment, the Kingdom is not the owner and this
      notice must not go out over its name.
- [ ] **Fair use has been genuinely considered, and the consideration is written
      down.** *Lenz v. Universal Music Corp.*, 815 F.3d 1145 (9th Cir. 2016),
      requires a copyright owner to form a subjective good faith belief that the
      use is not authorised by law — which includes 17 U.S.C. § 107 — before
      sending. Work the four factors in two or three sentences each, name the
      conclusion, sign it, and file it in the matter record. This step is not
      ceremony: it is the element the sender's own liability turns on, and a
      contemporaneous memorandum is the only proof that it happened.
- [ ] **The material has been captured and deposited in the Evidence Vault.** All
      four artefacts from `05-EVIDENCE-AND-CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY` § 2 — full-page
      capture showing URL and system clock, independent archival capture, the file
      itself with its SHA-256 digest, and the collector's contemporaneous note —
      with the custody record opened. Capture before you send. The material
      disappears within hours of the notice arriving, and a takedown with no
      preserved copy has destroyed the Kingdom's own evidence.
- [ ] **The correct designated agent has been identified.** Check the Copyright
      Office's DMCA Designated Agent Directory at dmca.copyright.gov first; a
      provider that has not designated an agent there has no safe harbour and no
      obligation, which changes the analysis. Where the service runs its own
      reporting process — a web form, a rights manager portal, a dedicated
      address — use it, because notices sent elsewhere are routinely discarded
      unread. Record which route was used and when.
- [ ] **Every URL has been checked on the day of sending** and resolves to
      infringing material. A stale or wrong URL is the commonest reason a notice
      is rejected, and an inaccurate one is the commonest route into § 512(f).
- [ ] **The registration position is known.** Registration number and effective
      date of registration recorded, or the § 412 three-month window checked
      against the date of first publication. See the playbook, § 2.
- [ ] **The Kingdom is prepared to sue on this work.** If a counter-notice
      arrives, the material returns in ten to fourteen business days unless suit
      is filed. Decide now, not then.
- [ ] **A legal hold has issued** and the Kingdom's own preservation duty is
      recognised as attached (`05-EVIDENCE-AND-CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY` § 7).
- [ ] **The matter is open in the Enforcement Docket** and the evidence linked to
      it.

## The notice

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD — name, postal address, telephone, email]

VIA [EMAIL TO agent@example.com / ONLINE FORM AT https://... / CERTIFIED MAIL]

Date: [DATE]

To:   Designated Agent for Notification of Claimed Infringement
      [SERVICE PROVIDER LEGAL NAME]
      [DESIGNATED AGENT NAME]
      [STREET ADDRESS]
      [CITY, STATE, ZIP]
      [EMAIL ADDRESS]

Re:   Notification of Claimed Infringement under 17 U.S.C. § 512(c)(3)(A)
      Our reference: [MATTER REFERENCE]

Dear Designated Agent:

I submit this notification under 17 U.S.C. § 512(c)(3)(A) on behalf of
[OWNER LEGAL NAME] ("the Owner"), the owner of the exclusive rights
identified below. This notification concerns material residing on your
system or network at the direction of a user within the meaning of
17 U.S.C. § 512(c). [FOR A SEARCH ENGINE OR DIRECTORY, SUBSTITUTE: This
notification concerns references or links to infringing material within
the meaning of 17 U.S.C. § 512(d).]

1. IDENTIFICATION OF THE COPYRIGHTED WORK CLAIMED TO HAVE BEEN INFRINGED

   Title:              [TITLE OF WORK]
   Type of work:       [LITERARY WORK / PICTORIAL OR GRAPHIC WORK /
                       SOUND RECORDING / MOTION PICTURE / OTHER]
   Author:             [AUTHOR NAME]
   Date of creation:   [DATE]
   First published:    [DATE] at [URL OR PLACE OF PUBLICATION]
   Registration:       U.S. Copyright Office Registration No. [NUMBER],
                       effective date of registration [DATE]
   The Owner's title:  [ORIGINAL AUTHORSHIP / WRITTEN ASSIGNMENT DATED
                       [DATE] / EXCLUSIVE LICENSE DATED [DATE]]

   An authorized copy of the work may be viewed at [URL].

   [WHERE MULTIPLE WORKS AT A SINGLE SITE ARE COVERED, SUBSTITUTE:
   The following is a representative list of the copyrighted works at the
   site identified in paragraph 2 that are covered by this notification:
   (a) [TITLE], Registration No. [NUMBER];
   (b) [TITLE], Registration No. [NUMBER];
   (c) [TITLE], Registration No. [NUMBER].]

2. IDENTIFICATION OF THE MATERIAL CLAIMED TO BE INFRINGING, AND
   INFORMATION REASONABLY SUFFICIENT TO PERMIT YOU TO LOCATE IT

   The following material is claimed to be infringing and is to be
   removed, or access to it disabled:

   (a) [FULL URL]
       Description: [WHAT APPEARS THERE — e.g., "the complete text of the
       work, reproduced without alteration, beginning 'It is hereby' and
       ending 'in perpetuity'"]
       Observed on: [DATE, TIME, TIME ZONE]

   (b) [FULL URL]
       Description: [DESCRIPTION]
       Observed on: [DATE, TIME, TIME ZONE]

   The material appears to have been posted by the account [HANDLE OR
   USERNAME], at [PROFILE URL], user identifier [NUMERIC ID IF KNOWN].

3. INFORMATION REASONABLY SUFFICIENT TO PERMIT YOU TO CONTACT THE
   COMPLAINING PARTY

   Name:      [OFFICER NAME]
   Office:    [OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
   Address:   [STREET ADDRESS, CITY, STATE, ZIP]
   Telephone: [NUMBER]
   Email:     [ADDRESS]

4. GOOD FAITH STATEMENT

   I have a good faith belief that use of the material in the manner
   complained of is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or
   the law.

5. STATEMENT OF ACCURACY AND AUTHORITY

   I state that the information in this notification is accurate, and,
   under penalty of perjury, that I am authorized to act on behalf of the
   owner of an exclusive right that is allegedly infringed.

6. SIGNATURE

   /s/ [FULL NAME]
   ______________________________
   [FULL NAME]
   [OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
   [DATE]

Please confirm receipt of this notification and advise what action has been
taken. I ask that you preserve the material identified above, the associated
account records, and the related access logs pending resolution of this
matter.

Nothing in this notification waives any right or remedy available to the
Owner, all of which are expressly reserved.

Respectfully,

[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[EMAIL] · [TELEPHONE]
```

## Notes

**The six elements are a checklist, not a style guide, and omission is fatal.** A
provider that receives a notice missing any element of § 512(c)(3)(A) owes nothing
and, under § 512(c)(3)(B)(i), the defective notice is not even considered in
determining whether the provider had knowledge of the infringement. Most rejected
notices fail on element two (no registration or no identifiable work) or element
three (a link to a home page rather than to the infringing item). Give exact URLs,
one per line.

**The two statements are different and must not be merged.** Element five is an
ordinary statement of good faith belief. Element six is sworn under penalty of
perjury — and what is sworn is *authority to act*, not the merits of the claim.
The template keeps them in separate numbered paragraphs for that reason. Sending
a notice that swears to the infringement itself enlarges the sender's exposure for
no benefit. Do not embellish the statutory language; the words "or the law" in
element five are the words that carry *Lenz*, and they must appear.

**Section 512(f) is real and it runs against the sender.** Any person who
knowingly materially misrepresents that material is infringing is liable for the
damages, including costs and attorney's fees, incurred by the alleged infringer,
by any copyright owner or licensee, or by the service provider, as a result of
relying on the misrepresentation. The standard is subjective knowledge rather than
negligence, which is protective — but the protection evaporates where the sender
took down material they knew they did not own, or plainly did not consider fair
use. The written fair-use memorandum in the checklist above is what stands between
a good faith error and a knowing misrepresentation.

**The counter-notice forces a decision within two weeks.** Under § 512(g)(3) the
poster may serve a counter-notice stating, under penalty of perjury, a good faith
belief that the material was removed as a result of mistake or misidentification,
and consenting to the jurisdiction of the federal district court where they
reside. The provider must then replace the material not less than ten nor more
than fourteen business days after receiving it, unless the Kingdom first notifies
the provider that it has filed an action seeking a court order restraining the
infringing activity. So the counter-notice is the moment the matter stops being
free. Do not send a notice on material the Kingdom would not litigate over, and
never on an unregistered work: § 411(a) and *Fourth Estate Publishing Ass'n v.
Wall-Street.com, LLC*, 586 U.S. 296 (2019), mean the suit could not be filed in
time even if the Kingdom wished to file it.

**Do not demand the poster's identity in this notice.** Subscriber identifying
information is obtained through a subpoena issued by the clerk of a United States
district court under 17 U.S.C. § 512(h), on a request accompanied by a copy of the
notification and a sworn declaration. Providers will not disclose it on request,
and asking makes the notice look like a fishing expedition.

**This notice will probably become public.** Many providers forward received
notices to the Lumen Database, where the sender's name, the works claimed, and the
URLs are indexed and searchable indefinitely. Write every line knowing it will be
read by strangers, and use an official address rather than a residential one.

**Register of choice.** The statutory quotations and the letter body use American
spelling and the statute's own phrasing, because the recipient is a United States
service provider reading against the text of § 512. The Kingdom's ordinary house
style governs everything outside the fenced block.

**What this template deliberately is not.** It is a notification by a rights
holder to a service provider under a federal statute. It bears no seal implying
judicial authority, styles itself as no form of process, commands nothing of the
poster, and asserts no jurisdiction over anyone. The provider is asked, not
ordered; the statute supplies the incentive. Keep it in that register.
